title: Map and key/value collections
learningObjectives: Explain map and key/value collections and use JavaScript collections and iteration safely.

understand.concept: Map stores key-value pairs and preserves insertion order. Keys can be any value, including objects and functions. Map offers set, get, has, delete, clear, and iteration methods; unlike ordinary objects, it has no inherited string-key properties in its entry collection.
understand.whyItMatters: Map is useful for dynamic key-value data and non-string keys. It makes the intent of a collection explicit and exposes its size directly.
understand.analogy: A Map is a labelled collection where each key points to one value.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; collection identity, iteration, and binary storage follow JavaScript specification rules.

explain.narrative: get retrieves a value by key; size counts entries; iteration yields key-value pairs in insertion order.

examples.explanation: get retrieves a value by key; size counts entries; iteration yields key-value pairs in insertion order.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the collection, iteration, or copying behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Use a Map keyed by course objects. Add, update, delete, and iterate entries, then compare with a plain object.
practise.independentTask: Choose an appropriate collection or iteration technique for a small data task. Test duplicates, ordering, identity, and copying behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates its receiver.
Remember that object equality is based on identity.
Use typed arrays only when binary data semantics are needed.

questions.prompt: Can a Map use an object as a key?
questions.explanation: Map keys may be values of any type, including objects.
